definition: Mundane means ordinary and commonplace — the plain, unexciting business of everyday life.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word mundane. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know mundane should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: She loved how the astronauts' checklists made orbit sound mundane: wipe the filter, log the reading, stow the trash.
Everyday is milder than mundane: everyday tasks are simply the normal round, stated without complaint, while calling them mundane adds the first sigh of dullness.
Humdrum goes further than mundane: a mundane job is merely unexciting, while a humdrum one drones — the sameness has thickened into wearying monotony.
Ordinary means unremarkable — a neutral report that nothing here stands out. Mundane adds a faint shrug of dullness: the flatness of chores, errands, and paperwork, felt as flatness.

Routine means done as a regular procedure, by habit or schedule. Mundane is about how uninteresting a thing feels, not how regularly it happens — a routine task can still thrill, and a mundane one can be a one-off.
